title: Variance-Aware Mini-Batch Orchestrator for Embeddings
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Introduce a variance-aware mini-batch orchestrator to reduce p99 tail latency and increase sustained throughput for the embeddings endpoint across heterogeneous tenant traffic patterns. The orchestrator combines short-term variance forecasting, micro-batch packing, and prioritized admission so that high-variance tenants do not disproportionately increase latency for other tenants.
background: Current embedding ingestion uses a single FIFO queue per pool with coarse-grained batching. We observed frequent p95/p99 spikes from tenants with bursty small requests and from variable sequence length distributions. Existing autoscalers react too slowly for short bursts and allocating more warm capacity is expensive. Previous tickets focused on admission control and burst buffers but did not combine per-tenant variance forecasting with dynamic micro-batch molding.
goals: 1) Reduce embedding p99 latency by at least 25% for mixed-tenant workloads. 2) Improve token/sec utilization of GPU pools by 10% during steady state. 3) Maintain or reduce cost per 1M tokens. 4) Provide configurable tenant QoS (low-latency vs cost-efficient) via labels. 5) Safe, incremental rollout with observability and rollback.
success_metrics: p50_p99_reduction: p99 <= previous_p99 * 0.75; throughput_utilization: >= previous_utilization * 1.1; cost_per_token: <= previous_cost_per_token; SLO_violations: <= 0.5x historical for targeted tenants
design_notes:
- Forecast short-term variance (30s window) per tenant using exponentially weighted moving variance on request inter-arrival and token-length.
- Maintain two admission lanes per pool: latency-priority (small micro-batches, tight timeout) and efficiency-priority (pack to larger batches).
- Micro-batch orchestrator continuously molds in-flight packing: attempt pack-up-to N requests or timeout T milliseconds; N and T are functions of forecast variance and target QoS.
- Token-aware packing: prefer packing requests whose combined token length fits efficient kernel sizes to reduce kernel fragmentation.
- Integrate with existing autoscaler signals: orchestrator exposes headroom metric (predicted short-term demand) to trigger faster warm-ups, and backoff signals when queue latency grows.
- Fallback: if instability detected (rising p99 or error rates), revert to current FIFO batching for affected pool and auto-create incident tag for oncall.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: Simulation and canary scheduler (2 weeks). Build discrete-event simulator using sampled production traces to validate packing and variance forecasting.
Phase 2: Implement orchestrator in serving runtime as opt-in scheduler behind feature flag (4 weeks). Add telemetry and headroom metric.
Phase 3: Canary on low-traffic orgs with synthetic burst tests (2 weeks). Tune N/T heuristics.
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 20%, 50%, 100% with per-tenant QoS labels (2-4 weeks).
Phase 5: Post-rollout evaluation and cleanup (2 weeks).
tasks: Build simulator and run against 30 days of embeddings trace
Design API for tenant QoS labels and sequencing hints
Implement variance estimator library in runtime
Add micro-batch orchestrator with two lanes
Expose headroom and backlog metrics to autoscaler
Create dashboards and alerts for p95/p99 and ordering regressions
Write runbook for rollback and incident response
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Simulator MVP completed. Initial sims show 18% p99 reduction on mixed traces when micro-batch packing is variance-informed.
2025-11-20: Design review with Serving and Autoscale teams. Agreed on headroom metric schema and backoff signals. Action: Lyndsey to prototype headroom exporter (PR #4531).
2025-12-01: Implemented variance estimator and unit tests. Edge cases for bursty single-request tenants covered. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4629.
2026-01-08: Canary scheduler implemented behind feature flag. Basic telemetry added to metrics pipeline (metric names: embeddings.orch.p99, embeddings.orch.headroom, embeddings.orch.queue_depth).

2026-02-05: Canary run on 3 selected tenants (internal) for 48 hours. Observed p99 reduction of 28% and 12% increased GPU utilization for those pools. Noted higher median latency for a single tenant mis-labeled as efficiency-priority; corrected QoS label list.
2026-03-02: Autoscaler integration test passed in staging. Headroom signal consumed by fast-warmup hook. Preparing production canary for 10% of traffic next week.
2026-03-10: Rollout plan approved by SRE and Product. Preparing runbook and dashboards.
review_feedback: 2025-11-20 (Serving lead - Jordan Blake): Prefer simple heuristics initially; avoid ML models in runtime. Keep forecast window small (<= 60s).
2025-12-02 (SRE - Maria Chen): Ensure headroom metric is rate-limited to avoid autoscaler thrash. Add safety cap to ramp rate.
2026-01-10 (PM - Carlos Rivera): Add config toggle per customer to opt into low-latency profile; expose in Console with warnings about cost.
2026-02-08 (Design - Priya Menon): Make sure observability surfaces tenant-specific traces for mini-batches to debug ordering anomalies.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Packing heuristics may create starvation for very large single-request tenants. Mitigation: fairness token that ensures any tenant with waiting request > X seconds gets priority lane for next N cycles.
Risk: Autoscaler thrash due to noisy headroom. Mitigation: add EWMA smoothing and min-cooldown.
Risk: Kernel inefficiencies due to mixed token lengths. Mitigation: token-aware packing and reject packs that cross inefficient boundaries more than Y% of the time.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary shows >=20% p99 reduction for targeted pools without increasing error rate. 2) Headroom metric consumed by autoscaler and causes warmups with <10% false positives. 3) No more than 1 rollback during 2-week ramp. 4) Console exposes per-tenant QoS toggle and docs updated.
notes_for_oncall: If p99 spikes >x2 during canary, immediately flip feature flag off for affected pool, page oncall and set incident tag 'orch-canary-rollback'. Check headroom and queue_depth metrics and attach logs linked from PR #4629.
postmortem_plan: If rollback occurs, run a 72-hour trace analysis, update simulator with failing traces, and schedule a follow-up retro with owning teams. Save artifacts to Confluence and update rollout checklist.
communication_plan: Weekly status in #infra-embeddings, biweekly sync with Product and SRE. Send canary start/end short report to stakeholders and update Console release notes when rolled out.
